Dr Climate Wiseman and KDC Uganda

Dr Climate Wiseman, also known on this website as Bishop Climate Wiseman, leads Kingdom Deliverance Centre Uganda. KDC is a church community in Kampala with worship, prayer and Bible teaching at the heart of its public gatherings. This introduction focuses on his connection with the church and the practical information visitors can use.

A church leader’s public introduction should help readers understand where the community gathers, how to participate and where to ask questions. For a detailed personal biography, ministry history or speaking enquiry, contact the KDC team directly so they can provide current information.

Meet the church community in Kampala

Kingdom Deliverance Centre is located at Kosovo Trading Centre in the Lungujja area of Kampala, Uganda. The congregation gathers for English and Luganda Sunday worship, giving visitors a choice of services as they plan their first visit.

The English service runs from 8:00 AM to 10:30 AM EAT. The Luganda service follows from 10:30 AM to 2:00 PM EAT. If you are unfamiliar with the area, allow time for your journey and ask the team about directions before travelling.

Teaching, prayer and monthly Fire Service

Wednesday Bible study takes place from 6:00 PM to 9:30 PM EAT. It offers another opportunity to engage with Scripture, bring questions and build a rhythm of learning alongside other believers. The sermon library also provides a way to explore teaching between gatherings.

Fire Service takes place on the last Friday of each month from 6:00 PM to 9:30 PM EAT. The calendar date changes each month, so use the current event listing when planning your journey. There is no need to rely on an older poster.

Take a practical next step

You can begin by attending worship, reading the church’s information or speaking with the ministry team. Ask about accessibility, attending with family and the service that best fits your plans. A conversation can help you arrive with a clearer understanding of what to expect.

Meet KDC Uganda, plan your visit or contact the church team. For monthly prayer gatherings, check the next Fire Service date.

content:
Dr Climate Wiseman ministry at KDC Uganda

Dr Climate Wiseman ministry at Kingdom Deliverance Centre Uganda brings together worship, biblical teaching and prayer in Kampala. This guide explains the church’s regular gatherings and the ways a visitor can begin participating. It focuses on practical church life rather than promising a particular personal outcome.

People approach church with different experiences and questions. Some are looking for a place to worship, others want to understand the teaching, and others would like someone to pray with them. Start with the information you need and speak with the team when you want further guidance.

Worship in English and Luganda

Sunday gatherings include an English service from 8:00 AM to 10:30 AM EAT and a Luganda service from 10:30 AM to 2:00 PM EAT. The venue is Kingdom Deliverance Centre at Kosovo Trading Centre in Lungujja, Kampala.

Choose a service that fits your language preference and travel arrangements. Bringing a Bible and a notebook can help you reflect on what you hear. If you are coming with children or need accessibility information, ask the church team before setting out.

Build a rhythm of learning and prayer

Wednesday Bible study runs from 6:00 PM to 9:30 PM EAT. Reading Scripture with other believers can help you notice context, ask careful questions and consider a practical response during the week. You can also browse the sermon library for teaching.

The monthly Fire Service is held on the last Friday from 6:00 PM to 9:30 PM EAT. Visit the Events page for the actual date and venue details. The Fire Service page also explains the prayer-list form.

Participate thoughtfully in church life

Getting involved can begin with a conversation rather than a large commitment. Ask what opportunities currently exist, how much time a role involves and what guidance is available. Your skills, interests and availability can help the team suggest an appropriate next step.

Church participation also includes ordinary acts of welcome, listening and care. Be considerate of other people’s privacy when sharing prayer concerns, and make commitments you can sustain. Explore church life or contact KDC Uganda to ask questions and plan your visit.

content:
Dr Climate Wiseman and the church’s public name

Dr Climate Wiseman is introduced by KDC Uganda as its church leader and founder. The name used throughout this website is Kingdom Deliverance Centre Uganda, often shortened to KDC Uganda. Visitors searching for the ministry can use that name when checking service information and contacting the team.

Knowing the church’s location and current schedule is a helpful starting point. KDC gathers at Kosovo Trading Centre in the Lungujja area of Kampala. This article introduces the community a visitor can meet there, with links to the pages that carry practical details.

What you can explore before visiting

Read the About page for an introduction to the church and its leadership. The sermon library offers teaching to explore, while the church blog includes guidance on prayer, studying the Bible and taking part in community life.

These resources can help you prepare questions of your own. You might want to ask about the language used in a service, how to reach the venue or opportunities to learn during the week. Contacting the team is useful when information needs confirming.

Choose your gathering and plan your journey

Sunday English worship runs from 8:00 AM to 10:30 AM EAT. Sunday Luganda worship runs from 10:30 AM to 2:00 PM EAT. Wednesday Bible study meets from 6:00 PM to 9:30 PM EAT, providing another setting for Scripture and shared learning.

Fire Service takes place monthly on the last Friday, from 6:00 PM to 9:30 PM EAT. Because the date changes, check the current event before travelling. Make a return-journey plan as well, especially when attending an evening gathering with family.

Connect at a pace that suits you

A first visit does not need to answer every question. Come ready to listen and observe, then introduce yourself when you feel comfortable. Ask where to find information and how to stay connected with the church during the week.

If you would like to serve, begin by describing your interests and realistic availability. If you want prayer support, use the published contact channels and avoid including unnecessary private information about other people. Plan your visit or speak with the KDC team about your next step.

title: The Code of the Spirit: Reading Biblical Numbers 1 to 5
meta_title: The Code of the Spirit: Reading Biblical Numbers 1 to 5
meta_description: Read The Code of the Spirit with a practical guide to biblical numbers 1 to 5. Explore context, symbolism and practical questions for Bible study at KDC Uganda.
excerpt: Read The Code of the Spirit with a practical guide to biblical numbers 1 to 5. Explore context, symbolism and practical questions for Bible study at KDC Uganda.
content:
The Code of the Spirit: begin with Scripture

The Code of the Spirit invites a conversation about numbers in the Bible. A thoughtful study begins with the passage itself: who is speaking, what is happening and how a number contributes to the surrounding account. Context helps us distinguish what the text says from an interpretation we bring to it.

Numbers can describe ordinary details, structure a story or form part of a wider pattern. Their significance should be considered within the particular passage. A number appearing in Scripture does not, by itself, establish a prediction about someone’s future or a rule for making everyday decisions.

Read numbers one, two and three in context

When reading a passage that uses one, ask whether it describes a person, an event, a quantity or an emphasis on unity. Look at the surrounding sentences before assigning a symbolic meaning. Write down the observation separately from your interpretation.

With two or three, use the same careful approach. Notice whether the text describes people acting together, repeated actions or a sequence of events. Compare related passages when appropriate, while allowing each passage to speak within its own setting and purpose.

Consider four and five without forcing a formula

Four and five may be part of a list, a measurement, a count or a narrative detail. Read the whole section and ask what its writer is communicating. Avoid assuming that every occurrence carries an identical hidden message.

A useful study question is whether your conclusion can be explained from the passage. If it depends mainly on an outside numerical system, identify that as an interpretation rather than presenting it as an explicit statement of Scripture. Discuss uncertainty openly and return to the text together.

Turn study into faithful daily practice

Bible study is more than solving a puzzle. Ask how the passage speaks about God, relationships, responsibility and the way we live. A practical response might involve honesty, patience, generosity, forgiveness or a decision to seek wise advice.

At KDC Uganda, Wednesday Bible study runs from 6:00 PM to 9:30 PM EAT. Bring your Bible and questions, listen respectfully and make room to learn. Plan a visit or explore the sermon library for further teaching and reflection.

content:
Kingdom Deliverance Centre Uganda: a message of hope

Kingdom Deliverance Centre Uganda uses the phrase “Where the captives are set free” to express its Christian message of hope and freedom in Jesus Christ. At KDC in Kampala, worship, prayer and biblical teaching form part of the church’s shared life. This introduction explains how visitors can explore that message and connect with the community.

People come to church with different questions, experiences and needs. Some want to learn about faith, while others are looking for a place to worship or people to pray with. You can begin with an honest conversation and take time to understand what the church teaches.

Worship with the church in Kampala

KDC meets at Kosovo Trading Centre in Lungujja, Kampala. Sunday English worship runs from 8:00 AM to 10:30 AM EAT, followed by Luganda worship from 10:30 AM to 2:00 PM EAT. Choose a service that fits your language preference and travel plans.

Allow time for the journey and bring a Bible or notebook if you find that helpful. If you have questions about accessibility, attending with children or finding the venue, contact the team before coming. Practical preparation can make a first visit more comfortable.

Make room for prayer and learning

Wednesday Bible study meets from 6:00 PM to 9:30 PM EAT. Studying Scripture with others can help you ask thoughtful questions, consider the context of a passage and reflect on how its teaching applies to everyday choices.

Fire Service is a monthly prayer gathering on the last Friday from 6:00 PM to 9:30 PM EAT. Check the current event for the actual date. You can prepare a short prayer list, including reasons for gratitude and the concerns you want to bring before God.

Take your next step with care

Christian growth involves learning over time. Prayer, reading Scripture, honest relationships and practical responsibility can support that journey. A gathering does not require you to claim a particular result or compare your experience with someone else’s story.

If you would like to participate, start with a visit or a question. Explore the About page, browse sermons or contact KDC Uganda. The Events page gives current gathering details, and the Prayer page offers a way to share a request.
